reviews.title: Misleading free trial and awful customer service
reviews.text:
I signed up believing I was getting the advertised seven-day free trial, only to be charged immediately. After contacting support, I was eventually told that the trial only applies to annual subscriptions, not monthly ones. This distinction certainly wasn’t clear to me when signing up.

What made the experience worse was the customer service. I had to explain the same issue repeatedly, received generic responses that completely missed the point, and was eventually addressed by someone else’s name. Rather than properly acknowledging my concerns, I was simply directed to Apple for a refund.

For an app that positions itself as an advocate for women’s health and wellbeing, the lack of care, transparency and understanding is particularly disappointing.

A terrible first impression. I certainly wouldn’t recommend it based on my experience.

reviews.title: Inaccurate Reports and 2 hour wait
reviews.text:
I've done so much tracking on this app. 4 years to be exact.
They don't have accurate graphs. Specifically they don't have the symptoms per cycle.
They have “most logged symptoms". So over four years of data... that information isn't what I want. I want per cycle what symptoms did I have. In what day or what phase.
When I inquired with customer service agent Medina. They said "this is the first time we've had feedback that the report feels unclear or not helpful in this way". Then when I asked to fill out a survey on this experience. They ignored my messages for 24 hours. Even while in a full conversation. I even started a new chat and they ignored that too for an hour and a half. Don’t recommend wasting your time inputting since you can’t get an accurate report for your information.

reviews.title: Warning! The app messed with my Apple Health data
reviews.text:
I’m sure the app works for some however I had problems linking it to Apple health data. I synced the Lively period tracker with my health app in the hopes of seamlessly transferring 6 years worth of cycle information. This was not the case. The information it uploaded after a simple syncing process was not correct and very skewed. It had lengthened periods, baring in mind I am usually regular, added spotting dates when there previously weren’t any, and also subsequently sent warnings that various lengths were irregular and ‘needed attention’. The only attention needed is for this bug to be fixed. When I went onto my original Apple health app, the data had been messed up there too. This was frustrating as I then spent valuable time trying to fix the data, helplessly trying to estimate what the actual dates were from 6 years ago! I have managed to correct them as much as I can but it will never be the real data which is upsetting - but I take accountability for relying solely on technology to track it. 

The actual Lively app seems nice and it offers what looks like good advice. 

However I don’t think it’s worth the subscription price for me. At the time of writing this I have only had the app a few hours and have now cancelled the free trial and deleted my account. (I better not get charged for it!!) 
I’ll be going back to the trusted Apple health app after this stressful and time consuming issue.

reviews.title: Not intuitive. No refund
reviews.text:
Used for less than a week and just didn’t like it. It’s not intuitive and not detailed enough. The widgets are not usable and I felt the only nice feature were the quotes/mantras. The app didn’t link to my Apple health cycle tracking either so basically had to track manually on multiple apps. 

Most frustration is the trial-to-buy. I signed up and missed the cancel deadline by one hour (same day, just didn’t know when the cut-off was!!). I tried to request a refund but unsuccessful. I really, really hate these automated pay-trials. After the trial, the demo should just end. Then give the option to sign up. Companies need to stop stealing from people like that. Now I have paid for an app I won’t ever use. Great.
